comments.body:
Implementation pushed for review as Gerrit change 1650 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1650), commit 94a537e2aa.

SHAPE CHOSEN: distinct journal patterns into distinct METRIC NAMES, not a CloudWatch dimension. observability.sh §4e reuses the existing publish_autodeploy_marker_delta helper (whose first argument is already an ERE handed to grep -cE) with two new offset files, emitting review_interrupts_bound_exceeded and review_interrupts_signal_unavailable alongside the UNCHANGED rolled-up review_interrupts. Everything stays dimensionless on both sides, so the monitoring_s4b.tf silent-unmatch hazard cannot bite (AC3 holds trivially). monitoring_autodeploy.tf replaces the single alarm with one alarm per reason, each carrying only its own remediation; the rolled-up metric is still published but no longer alarmed, so an interrupt never double-pages.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: re-tuning bound-exceeded's sensitivity. Both alarms keep the pre-split 900s / 1-datapoint / Sum > 0 / notBreaching cadence, so the split changes no sensitivity and signal-unavailable still latches on one datapoint (AC2). Making bound-exceeded quieter belongs with the DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX disposition, not here.

COORDINATION: kept disjoint from bug 2dc7 (affluent-conveyable-dromedary, Gerrit 1648), which rewrites the negative-delta clamp INSIDE the helpers. My edits are the comment block, the offset-file declarations and the call sites; the helper's offset/clamp logic is untouched. Verified against 1648's current diff — no overlapping lines.

VERIFICATION (no host shell access needed for any of it): new tests/scripts/test_observability_interrupt_reasons.py drives the REAL observability.sh over a synthetic unit journal, including the piranha case itself — four firings that are ALL bound-exceeded leave review_interrupts_signal_unavailable at 0, which is exactly the discrimination 7b4a needed SSM for. 28 passed across the new file plus test_observability_offsets_6a65.py, test_observability_exit.py and test_autodeploy_review_drain.py. terraform fmt -check and terraform validate both clean — validate caught a real constraint on the way, CloudWatch caps alarm_description at 1024 chars, and both descriptions were tightened under it; CI's terraform-drift workflow runs the same two checks.

STILL OPEN: AC4. This is a Terraform alarm-contract change and takes effect only on an operator terraform apply, not on merge.

comments.body:
MERGED — but this ticket stays OPEN, because its last AC is an operator action I cannot perform.

Gerrit change 1650 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1650) merged with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1, and landed on origin/main as 5a3ad479f0 (Gerrit rebased it server-side onto c9234694e0).

WHAT IS TRUE AS OF MERGE:
- AC1 (distinguishable without host shell) — CODE LANDED. observability.sh 4e emits review_interrupts_bound_exceeded and review_interrupts_signal_unavailable as separate metrics; monitoring_autodeploy.tf declares rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts-bound-exceeded and rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts-signal-unavailable, each carrying only its own remediation. EFFECTIVE ONLY AFTER APPLY (see below).
- AC2 (signal-unavailable stays prompt) — LANDED. Its alarm keeps period=900, evaluation_periods=1, datapoints_to_alarm=1, threshold=0, GreaterThanThreshold, notBreaching. Identical to the pre-split cadence, so the split changed no sensitivity in either direction.
- AC3 (dimensions agree both sides) — LANDED. No dimension anywhere: the split is by metric NAME, so the monitoring_s4b.tf silent-unmatch hazard is structurally impossible here rather than merely avoided. A test asserts no --dimensions is ever passed.
- AC4 (rolled-up total still published) — LANDED. review_interrupts is published unchanged, so pre-split history stays readable and any future third reason is still counted; it is no longer ALARMED, so a single interrupt cannot double-page.
- AC5 (proven by an automated test) — LANDED. tests/scripts/test_observability_interrupt_reasons.py drives the real observability.sh over a synthetic unit journal. It includes the piranha case as a named test: four firings that are ALL bound-exceeded leave review_interrupts_signal_unavailable at 0 — the exact discrimination 7b4a-0f39-1a45-4ce9 needed SSM shell access for. Re-verified on the landed tree at 5a3ad479f0: 14 passed, terraform fmt -check and terraform validate both clean.
- AC6 (applied, not merely merged, and recorded) — NOT SATISFIED. THIS IS WHAT KEEPS THE TICKET OPEN.

OPERATOR ACTION REQUIRED — terraform apply in infra/terraform.

Until that apply runs, NOTHING about alarming has actually changed on the account, and the intermediate state is worth understanding before someone reads a dashboard and draws the wrong conclusion:
- The host probe starts publishing the two new metrics as soon as the new observability.sh reaches the box via autodeploy — that half needs no apply.
- But the ALARMS are still the old single rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts on the rolled-up metric. So between merge and apply, behaviour is exactly as before: an interrupt pages once, without a reason. Nothing regresses, nothing improves.
- After apply, the old alarm is REPLACED by the two new ones. Expect the old alarm name to disappear from the console; that is intended, not an accident, and it is the only destructive part of the plan.
- The two new alarms will read INSUFFICIENT_DATA until their first datapoint, then settle to OK via treat_missing_data = notBreaching.

I did not run terraform apply and deliberately did not attempt to: this ticket is observability-only and I have no mandate to mutate live infrastructure. Please re-open this comment thread with the apply output (or a plan diff) once it has run, and then AC6 is satisfiable and the ticket can close.

COORDINATION NOTE: bug 2dc7 (affluent-conveyable-dromedary, Gerrit 1648, marker counters recounting on rotation) was still open when 1650 landed. The two changes are disjoint by construction — 1648 rewrites the negative-delta clamp INSIDE the publish helpers, this change touches only the comment block, the offset-file declarations and the call sites — but 1648 now needs a rebase over 5a3ad479f0. Its clamp change will apply to the two new reason counters automatically, since they go through the same helper.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`rebar/host:review_interrupts` is published DIMENSIONLESS, but `autodeploy.sh` emits its
`AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT` marker for two causes with a `reason` field that the metric
throws away:

- `bound-exceeded`   — `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX` was spent with reviews still in flight. The bot is
                       busy; the drain check is WORKING.
- `signal-unavailable` — `/health`'s `in_flight` was unreadable, so the deploy ran WITHOUT a
                       drain check. The probe itself is broken and every deploy is blind.

These have OPPOSITE remediations, and the alarm cannot tell them apart.

## Why this is worth its own ticket

This is the concrete cost, not a hypothetical. [rebar:7b4a-0f39-1a45-4ce9] was filed by an
automated CloudWatch sweep that could see the firings but not their reason, so it had to hedge
between "the bot is busy" and "34cd has silently regressed and every deploy is blind" — and its
own AC1 was "read the reason from `journalctl` on the box". Answering it required SSM shell
access to i-00880b2c7f13527c5. It turned out to be `bound-exceeded` on all four firings, but
that could not be known from the metric.

The alarm description in `monitoring_autodeploy.tf` already tells the investigator to go read
the journal for the reason field. Splitting the metric removes that hop, and matters most for
`signal-unavailable`, which is the urgent one and is currently indistinguishable from routine
burst residue.

## Scope — observability only, but it needs an apply

Behaviour-preserving for autodeploy and for reviews: nothing about deferral, the bound, or
review execution changes. It is confined to how the existing marker is counted and alarmed.
`autodeploy.sh` is NOT edited: it already stamps the reason.

## Implementation plan

**Chosen shape: distinct journal patterns counted into separate DIMENSIONLESS metrics**, not a
CloudWatch dimension. This mirrors how `observability.sh` §4e already keeps `deploy_deferrals`
separate from `review_interrupts`, and it sidesteps the standing hazard that a dimension added
on only one side silently unmatches (monitoring_s4b.tf). Dimensionless on both sides therefore
holds trivially.

1. `infra/scripts/observability.sh` §4e — add two offset files
   (`INTERRUPT_BOUND_OFFSET_FILE`, `INTERRUPT_SIGNAL_OFFSET_FILE`) and two extra calls to the
   EXISTING `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` helper, whose first argument is already an ERE
   passed to `grep -cE`. The markers are JSON (`AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT {"ts": …, "reason":
   "bound-exceeded", …}`), so the patterns are the token plus the quoted reason field. Emits:
   - `review_interrupts_bound_exceeded`
   - `review_interrupts_signal_unavailable`
   - `review_interrupts` (UNCHANGED rolled-up total — existing history stays readable and a
     future third reason is still counted somewhere).
   The helper's offset/publish/clamp logic is NOT touched (bug 2dc7 owns that seam).
2. `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf` — replace the single `review_interrupts` alarm
   with two reason-scoped alarms (`rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts-bound-exceeded`,
   `…-signal-unavailable`), each on its own metric, each keeping today's
   900s/1-datapoint/`Sum > 0`/`notBreaching` cadence, so aggregate sensitivity is preserved and
   `signal-unavailable` still latches on a single datapoint. Each alarm description carries only
   ITS OWN remediation. The rolled-up metric keeps being published but is no longer alarmed, so
   a firing never double-pages. Re-tuning `bound-exceeded` to be less noisy is deliberately NOT
   done here — it belongs with the deferral-bound disposition.
3. New test `tests/scripts/test_observability_interrupt_reasons.py` — drives the real
   `observability.sh` with a stubbed `journalctl`/`aws` (same harness shape as
   `test_observability_offsets_6a65.py`, which is left untouched) over a mixed journal of
   bound-exceeded and signal-unavailable markers, and asserts the three published values split
   correctly and that the rolled-up total equals their sum.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_interrupt_reasons.py tests/scripts/test_observability_offsets_6a65.py`
  (the second proves the untouched offset behaviour did not regress).
- `terraform fmt -check` / `terraform validate` on `infra/terraform`.
- No host shell access is needed for any of the above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A future CloudWatch-only sweep can tell `bound-exceeded` from `signal-unavailable`
      WITHOUT shell access to the host: two distinctly-named metrics and two distinctly-named
      alarms exist, each with a single reason's remediation in its description.
- [ ] `signal-unavailable` remains promptly alarming (it is the "deploys are running blind"
      case): its alarm keeps `evaluation_periods = 1` / `datapoints_to_alarm = 1`.
- [ ] Metric and alarm agree on dimensions on both sides (both DIMENSIONLESS).
- [ ] A rolled-up `review_interrupts` is still published so pre-split history stays readable.
- [ ] The split is proven by an automated test that runs the real script — not by reading it.
- [ ] The Terraform change is applied, not merely merged, and that is recorded. **This AC is
      the operator's `terraform apply`; the implementing agent cannot satisfy it, so the ticket
      stays OPEN with the merged change recorded until the apply happens.**

file_impact.reason: split the AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT counter into per-reason metrics alongside the rolled-up total
replace the single review_interrupts alarm with two reason-scoped alarms
new test proving the per-reason split against the real script

compiled_state.title: split review_interrupts by reason so a CloudWatch-only sweep can tell bound-exceeded from signal-unavailable
